jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Are you the kind of person who makes complex things work smoothly? The person who walks into a room of competing priorities and finds the path forward? Who builds trust across teams, champions safety without being asked and leaves every environment a little more capable than they found it? If that sounds like you, keep reading. What you'll actually be doing and why it matters At Bristol Myers Squibb , the medicines we make change lives. And behind every batch, every stability study, every regulatory submission, there's a GMP laboratory environment that has to be safe, ready, and performing at its best - every single day. That's where you come in. As our GMP Laboratory Operations Lead for Building 6 , will sit at the heart of our Moreton site's Analytical Science and Operations team - connecting three distinct laboratory organisations (Analytical Leadership & Testing, Long Term Stability, and Marketed Life Stability) into a cohesive, high-performing whole. You'll be the person who makes sure the right conversations happen at the right time, that resources are aligned before they become a problem, that safety is embedded in the culture - not just the paperwork - and that when an auditor walks through our doors, we're more than ready to welcome them. This is a role where your impact is visible, broad, and lasting. Here's what a typical week might look like You're facilitating the Building 6 Laboratory Leadership Team - bringing ALT, LTS and MLS together to align on priorities, navigate competing demands, and make joined-up decisions that keep the labs moving forward You're working alongside GMP Laboratory Systems to make sure equipment qualification, calibration and maintenance activities are planned around operational needs - not in spite of them You're delivering hands-on training on a new analytical technique to a scientist who's just picked it up, making sure it sticks rather than being a one-off demo You're coaching an early-career scientist who's just taken on their first safety rep role, helping them find their voice and build their confidence You're leading a cross-functional discussion on lessons learned from a recent near-miss - turning it into a genuine improvement, not just a tick-box exercise You're preparing your teams for an upcoming regulatory inspection - not in a scramble, but calmly, because you've built a culture of readiness No two days are the same. And that's exactly the point. What you'll gain from this role Real influence, without needing a title to back it up. This role is built around matrix leadership - which means you'll develop and demonstrate one of the most valued skills in modern organisations: the ability to bring people with you through trust, clarity and collaboration rather than hierarchy. Breadth that builds your career. You'll work across laboratory operations, EHS, quality, capability development, infrastructure and strategic planning. That kind of cross-functional exposure is rare and it positions you brilliantly for senior leadership roles in science, operations or quality. A community, not just a job. You'll be the cultural anchor for the Building 6 laboratory community. You'll mentor apprentices and graduates, champion emerging scientists and leaders and actively shape the kind of environment people want to come to work in. That legacy matters - to them, and to you. A seat at the table where it counts. When the site faces its biggest operational challenges - resource pressure, regulatory scrutiny, infrastructure change - you'll be in the room. You won't be waiting to hear what was decided; you'll be part of making the decision. Visible impact on patient outcomes. Everything you do - keeping labs audit-ready, driving continuous improvement, building safety culture - directly enables the science that gets medicines to patients. That connection is real and it's something you'll feel every day. What you'll bring You don't need to have done this exact role before but you do need to bring: Solid GMP laboratory experience - you understand the regulated environment deeply and you've operated within it successfully A track record of working across complex, matrixed organisations - you know how to navigate ambiguity and align stakeholders without it becoming exhausting for everyone involved A genuine passion for safety - not as a compliance obligation but as something you personally believe in and actively promote The ability to influence without authority - people follow your lead because you earn it, not because an org chart says so Experience driving change and improvement - you've seen what good looks like and you know how to take others on the journey with you A scientific degree or equivalent hands-on experience - the credibility to be taken seriously in a highly technical environment The bigger picture BMS is on a mission to transform patients' lives through science. Our Moreton site is a critical part of that mission and Building 6 is at the heart of how we maintain the quality and safety standards that make it possible. This role isn't just about keeping the lights on. It's about building something - a laboratory community that's safer, more capable, more connected, and more ready for the future than it was before you arrived. If you're ready to lead with influence, develop with purpose, and make a tangible difference to the people around you and the patients we ultimately serve - we'd love to hear from you. #LI-Hybrid We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. The role is working within our studio: PuzzlePlay
Puzzleplay is Tripledot’s new player rewards platform, designed to make playing our games even more fun and engaging. By playing our casual, free to play mobile games, users can earn points, complete challenges, and win real prizes. It’s our way of giving back to players and rewarding them for doing what they already love. Puzzleplay is a key part of our growth strategy, combining smart engagement mechanics with high-quality game content.
Role Overview
Puzzleplay at Tripledot Studios is looking for a data analyst to own the fraud side of its user segmentation work. The team is building a system that combines fraud and activity signals to understand users and inform revenue-share decisions. You'll work with the analyst responsible for gameplay signals, alongside product and data colleagues, to keep that system useful as fraud patterns change.
Fraud patterns keep changing, so you'll regularly revisit the signals behind the segments and help the product team decide which verification methods make sense in each market.
This role is open to candidates based in Europe; Warsaw is preferred, where several of the people you'll work with are based.
Key Responsibilities
Review fraud signals regularly, adding, removing and refining them to distinguish suspicious activity from legitimate users. Signals under consideration include IP spoofing, VPN use and unusual play patterns.
Own the fraud-related segments of the user segmentation system, from deciding how signals should be interpreted to monitoring how well the categories work over time.
Work with the product team on fraud verification tools for different markets. The team currently uses FaceTec for facial verification and may need other methods, such as ID scanning or phone verification, in other countries.
Investigate users flagged for manual review, including ambiguous cases in the Tremendous queue, and look for ways to improve the review process.
Identify gaps in the available signals and recommend third-party tools for the product roadmap where they would help.
Required Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
Hands-on experience using data to investigate fraud and shape detection or prevention decisions, not just working alongside a fraud team.
Experience designing or improving fraud signals, user segments or review processes, with an interest in how those decisions change as tactics evolve.
The ability to work with product and other teams to turn analysis into operational fraud controls.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America. Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy.
